notes.decision: Translated 'as they hasten at every hour.' ⲧⲡⲏⲧ here circumstantial of ⲡⲱⲧ 'run, hasten' applied to men's restless activity in the world — fitting the chapter's theme of the three works for which Christians are sown in the world.

Translated 'set their hand upon him' as best literal sense. The verbal element ⲩⲝⲧ is unidentified — possibly Lyc. reflex of a 'set/stretch/apply' verb (perhaps ⲡⲱⲣⲕ̄ 'draw out' or ⲱⲣⲕ̄ 'swear/bind'). Idiom ⲧⲟⲟⲧϥ̄ ⲁⲣⲁ⸗ 'his hand upon (someone)' is well-attested for laying-hands gestures.
Read as ⲁ-ϥ-ⲥⲙⲛ̄ⲧ-ϩ '(she/he) established him' (Lyc. perfect with object suffix). The subject is feminine or matches some prior referent in lost context. Perfect of ⲥⲙⲓⲛⲉ/ⲥⲙⲟⲛⲧ 'establish.'

Translated 'But I — the Anointed who is seated in your midst.' ⲇⲛⲁⲕ ⲁⲉ read as scribal/dialectal variant of ⲁⲛⲁⲕ ⲇⲉ 'But I' (with metathesis). The construction parallels 2 Cor 13:3 (Paul's claim that Christ speaks within him), which fits the apostolic-voice register of this passage.

Translated 'do the work-of-the-doer.' The compound ⲙⲛⲧ-ⲁ(ⲩ/ϩ)ⲓⲣⲉ is the abstract of ⲣⲉϥⲣ̄ϩⲱⲃ 'doer/laborer' or related to ⲟⲩⲱⲓⲉ 'farmer' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲉ 'the farmer'). Given the immediately preceding seed-sowing imagery (line 10-11), the agricultural reading 'do the farmer's work / labor' is likely. Translated neutrally as 'work-of-the-doer' to preserve the abstract construction. Cf. 1 Cor 15:10 'I labored more abundantly than they all.'

Translated 'a good seedling.' ⲥⲓⲧ = 'sowing, seedling'; ⲛⲟⲩϩⲉ likely Lyc. for ⲛⲟⲩϥⲉ 'good' (cf. ⲛⲁϥⲣⲉ in glossary). Alternative: 'seed of the sycomore' (Sah. ⲛⲟⲩϩⲉ 'sycomore') is possible but less likely in this paraenetic context. The seed/seedling doublet ⲥⲡⲉⲣⲙⲁ ⲙⲛ̄ ⲥⲓⲧ matches Greek/Coptic agricultural pairings.

Translated 'shall be joined-together with me as fellow-heir.' ϩⲁⲱⲱⲧⲉ likely = ϣⲁ-ⲱⲱⲧ-ⲉ 'shall be joined' (qualitative of ⲱⲱⲧ 'be united, be one') functioning future-modally, paired with the Greek loanword ⲕⲗⲏⲣⲟⲛⲟⲙⲟⲥ 'heir.' Alternative: ϩⲁ-ⲱⲱⲧⲉ as preposition + noun. Echoes Romans 8:17 'fellow-heirs with Christ.'
